Sofia (customer): Hey, hitting intermittent failures when using streaming JSON mode. The client gets a truncated JSON payload about 1-2% of the time and the parser throws 'Unexpected end of input'.
Sofia (customer): We're streaming a large array of objects (~20k items), using stream=true and response_format=json. Example last chunk we see: 
```
{"data":[{"id":1,...},{"id":2,...},"id":3" : { ... }
# <-- stream stops here, no closing ] or }
```
Sofia (customer): curl request (redacted):
```bash
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxx' -d '{"model":"rdw-large","stream":true,"mode":"json"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Maya (Support): Sorry about that — can you paste the request_id from the response headers or the time (UTC) for one of the failures? Also which model and region?
Sofia (customer): request_id: rwd-req-20250318-09. Got two failure times: 2025-03-18T09:12:13Z and 2025-03-18T09:45:07Z. Model rdw-large, region us-west-2.
Jamal (Eng): Thanks — this looks like stream truncation mid-chunk. Can you confirm whether your client is using an HTTP/1.1 long-poll or HTTP/2 streaming? Also any proxy / ALB in front?
Sofia (customer): HTTP/1.1 chunked response through our internal edge (ALB-ish) and then a company proxy. No client-initiated cancel. Client just waits and then JSON.parse fails.
Rachel (SRE): I pulled the logs for rwd-req-20250318-09. Both failures show an upstream error: worker-17 returned ECONNRESET during write. There are intermittent 502s with connection reset by peer while streaming. Trace: trace-7f3a.
Nate (Infra): We recently tightened idle timeouts on the edge proxy to 30s for keepalives. If there's a long gap between flushes, the proxy may close the connection mid-stream. With chunked streaming that manifests as partial JSON on the client.
Jamal (Eng): Repro idea: produce a long-running response that sends a big JSON array but flushes infrequently (every ~40s). Client and proxy keepalives will conflict. If proxy kills at 30s, you'll get a truncated final chunk.
Maya (Support): Possible workarounds for customers: 1) disable streaming for structured JSON (non-streaming returns full JSON reliably), 2) stream but add frequent small flushes (heartbeat) from the server every 10s, 3) append a small sentinel token at the end of the JSON to help parsers detect truncation.
Sofia (customer): We can't easily change the proxy policy. Can you emit a sentinel from the API? Something like a final event: {"__rwd_stream_end__":true} so our parser can detect truncation and retry?
Jamal (Eng): We're hesitant to change protocol surface, but we can emit a terminating sentinel in streaming-json mode for a patch release. Short-term we suggest adding a client-side streamer that collects chunks and only attempts parse after a final 2s idle window or receiving an explicit EOF.
Rachel (SRE): Also, we've seen HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1 differences. If your stack downgraded, the chunk boundaries and flush semantics differ. We recommend trying HTTP/2 if possible.
Nate (Infra): Long-term fix: revert the edge keepalive change or proxy bump to 90s for streaming routes and add active keepalive pings. Short-term we can add server-side heartbeats (
`:
` event) every 10s to keep ALBs from closing.
Sofia (customer): Tested adding a 10s client-side timeout buffer and now errors dropped from 2% to ~0.05%. Still saw 1 final case where the stream cut inside a number literal.
Maya (Support): Can you share the raw last 1KB you received for that final case?
Sofia (customer): Pasted it: `{"data":[{...},{...},{"id":1234,"text":"...\`
Maya (Support): Ugh. That is clearly mid-byte cutoff. Jamal, any server-side logs for that exact timestamp?
Jamal (Eng): Looking at worker-17 at 2025-03-18T09:45:07Z — socket write returned EPIPE after 12.3s of sending. No explicit error in app layer. It looks like the TCP connection dropped from the proxy. We can add a finalizing flush that writes a small 1-2 byte token after the last JSON byte which will reduce the chance of truncation at chunk boundaries.
Nate (Infra): We'll also add a streaming route flag to keep ALB/proxy timeouts longer for customers that opt into streaming-json.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary streaming-sentinel to staging (build rwd/stream-sentinel-20250318).
Maya (Support): Sofia — can you try staging? It emits final sentinel `{"__rwd_stream_end__":true}` as a separate chunk after the JSON closes. Should be a safe additive change.
Sofia (customer): Trying staging now...
Sofia (customer): Good news — after 100k streamed objects in staging the sentinel arrived every time, client parse is stable. No truncation observed in 2000 runs. :tada:
Maya (Support): Great. We'll schedule the sentinel for a gradual rollout to prod and include docs for migrating parsers.
Jamal (Eng): Action items: 1) prod rollout with canary next 48h, 2) add docs + best-practice section on streaming structured output, 3) infra to relax keepalive for streaming routes.
Rachel (SRE): I'll monitor for any increase in proxied connection counts. Nate, please coordinate ALB config change.
Nate (Infra): On it. Will open the infra ticket and link back here.
Sofia (customer): Thanks team — much better now. We'll leave it running and report if anything else pops up.
Maya (Support): Closing this thread once prod rollout completes. Thanks everyone. :heart:
